messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High 5xx rate + timeouts observed for private-vpc-prod-eu-west. Alert group: networking-gateway. Pager: alice (oncall).

alice (oncall): I'm on it, joining console now. seeing spikes in 502/504 from gateway tier.

ben (sre): jumped in — metrics look like a sudden jump at 12:07 UTC: gateway error rate 502=18% -> 42% in 5m, latency p95 doubled.

carla (neteng): possible networking change? any recent SG/route changes pushed to prod VPCs?

alice (oncall): checking Terraform history... (grep) seems there was a change 11:58 UTC to tighten egress rules for env:private-prod (PR #3421) by infra-team.

ben (sre): that matches. flow logs show lots of REJECT on ephemeral ports 32768-61000 from NAT subnets -> egress to internet. If ephemeral ports are blocked, connections to downstream model endpoints stall and get 5xx.

carla (neteng): oh no. The PR constrained egress to only 80/443 by mistake; we need ephemeral range allowed for SNAT.

alice (oncall): can we revert that rule? who can patch quickly?

carla (neteng): I can revert. Rolling back SG egress to allow 32768-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0 for the NAT SG. Doing a manual change now and will push a safe fix in TF after.

deploy-bot: Applied change: security-group sg-0a12b3c4: egress update (allow 32768-65535 -> 0.0.0.0/0) by carla. (run-id: deploy-1867453250)

alice (oncall): observing traffic -- error rate dropping, p50 latency recovering. customers still impacted for a few requests in-flight.

dave (support): Customer escalations: 3 customers reported 502s on their private deployments around 12:10 UTC. Shared temporary mitigation note to them.

ben (sre): confirm from NAT metrics: ephemeral port exhaustion was trending up before change. After allowing ephemeral range, port usage freed and NAT retry rates dropped.

carla (neteng): root cause: recent tightening of egress SG removed ephemeral range. This blocked SNAT ephemeral ports causing upstream connections to fail at gateway layer. Also noticed one NAT instance in the pool hit connection table limits earlier (conntrack high) — probably amplified impact.

alice (oncall): immediate mitigation steps done: 1) reverted SG egress to include ephemeral range (manual) 2) added an extra NAT gateway in eu-west (hotfix) to spread load 3) scaled NAT EC2 worker pool (where applicable) to cool off conntrack.

ben (sre): commands used for debugging:
```
# flow logs quick-check
aws ec2 describe-flow-logs --filter Name=resource-id,Values=vpc-0abcde12345
# list recent SG change
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0a12b3c4
# check NAT instance conntrack (on NAT instances only)
sudo ss -s | grep "estab" && sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
```

carla (neteng): I've opened PR #3430 which re-applies proper egress rules and adds a test to prevent removing ephemeral port ranges. Also adding a policy to block direct manual pushes to SGs without a canary.

alice (oncall): status update for page: error rate down to baseline (~1%), latency normalizing. The incident is mitigated. Moving to post-incident review.

dave (support): sending customer follow-up template now with timeline and mitigation steps. Will include ETA for RCA.

ben (sre): suggested follow-ups (postmortem items):
- add automated check in CI to detect removal of ephemeral egress ranges for NAT-related SGs
- instrument NAT connection table metrics and alert when conntrack > 75%
- update runbook: "NAT egress 5xx" with clear rollback steps and TF safe patch instructions
- add a synthetic test that opens many outbound ephemeral connections to catch regressions

carla (neteng): will own the infra PR and add the CI test.

alice (oncall): handoff to ben for deeper RCA and runbook updates. I will file the incident ticket and draft the timeline.

ben (sre): taking handoff. final notes: total customer-impact window ~12:07-12:18 UTC (~11 minutes), primary root cause SG egress change, secondary amplifier: NAT conntrack/port pressure.

incident-bot: Incident status changed to RESOLVED (mitigated). Incident ID: INC-2026-1872.

alice (oncall): adding slack reactions :thumbsup: to the fix. Thanks everyone — we'll review in the postmortem tomorrow.

dave (support): I'll follow up with customers and close any outstanding tickets.

carla (neteng): PR linking: #3430 (fix + CI), tracking task INFRA-529 to add NAT autoscale & alerts.

ben (sre): closing thread; will attach metrics and timeline to incident ticket.
